features.text: The patient is a 66-year-old male.
The patient has had constant pain in his left shoulder and left elbow for about five months.
The pain is described as a constant ache, but can become sharper when moving the arm in certain ways.
The pain does not involve swelling, redness, numbness, or tingling.
The pain is localized to the left shoulder and elbow and does not radiate to other areas.
The patient fell five months ago while walking on icy stairs, landing on his left side, which likely caused the injury.
The patient has not undergone any imaging studies or consultations with a specialist for this condition.
The patient has been managing the pain with ice and rest, but it has not improved.
The pain worsens when lifting objects, especially weights at the gym.
The patient has limited range of motion in his left arm, especially when raising it overhead or twisting it.
The patient has not noticed any weakness in his left arm.
The patient has not experienced any clicking, popping, or locking in the shoulder or elbow.
The patient has not had any imaging studies such as X-rays or MRI for his shoulder or elbow pain.
